chunk_map.heading: H1/lede: Prep the run, fill the gaps
Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off
Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice
Phase 2: Build the ranked list of what will hurt the agent
Correct the list and reprioritise it
Fill the worst two or three gaps
Match each fill to its shape and home
Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase
Compare notes, then tidy the folder

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.fix_hint: chunk 7 "Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase" is single-bullet (17 words) but carries one concrete, self-carrying instruction — not a wait-state stub. Same family as chunks 2 and 4, already this short in the file's audited state.

Re-verified per the prior finding: chunk 7's header now covers only the surviving single bullet (no leftover callout/tidy content) — the 2026-08-12 re-chunk resolved it. Chunk 8's header "Compare notes, then tidy the folder" is a two-part header for two-part content: "Compare notes" maps to the time-check callout's "share what surfaced, where the audit missed, and why the agent sometimes goes lazy"; "tidy the folder" maps verbatim to the bullet's own "tidy the folder" lead. Both halves are covered, no residual.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
